look_here_first: Look for BROAD, FLAT spoon/obovate fleshy leaves with round or slightly notched tips and inconspicuous hairs at successive axils. Mature fruits open with a HORIZONTAL detachable lid but have NO expanded encircling wing like P. umbraticola. P. pilosa has narrow, near-cylindrical leaves and conspicuous long white axillary hair tufts. Yellow flower color is secondary.

project_inclusion.learner_admission_basis: Live Master Plant Pool row 925; personal iNaturalist Flora taxon 58991; approved source-pool learner admission.
project_inclusion.range_basis: Flora of North America explicitly lists Portulaca oleracea as introduced across North America including Texas. Kew POWO maps native range primarily Old World. Broad cosmopolitan species complex has debated historical origin; do not count as locally verified target-zone native.

morphology_keys.habit: Prostrate/spreading often reddish succulent annual, low mat-forming stems, short taproot.
morphology_keys.leaves: Flattened obovate or spatulate leaves generally 4–28 × 2–13 mm, apex round to shallowly notched; alternate to subopposite at nodes.
morphology_keys.flowers: Small flowers typically 3–10 mm diam with short yellow petals; ephemeral, often sunshine opening; don't ID by flower color.
morphology_keys.fruits: Ovoid unwinged circumscissile capsule usually 4–9 mm diam, 'hat/lid' detaches transversely to release many black/brown flattened seeds.
morphology_keys.seeds: Dark seeds around 0.6–1.1 mm with granular or rounded-tuberculate cells; macro needed for fine seed-coat differentiation.
morphology_keys.axils: Glabrous or only short inconspicuous trichomes around inflorescence/nodes.
best_field_traits: Broad, flattened spoon-like succulent leaves (not narrow terete).
Unwinged mature capsule with transverse cap-like lid; photograph opened and unopened fruit.
Short or absent axillary hairs at multiple fresh stem nodes.
Distinguish overlapping flat-leaved P. umbraticola using actual mature capsule wing.
Do not use reddish stem, prostrate growth or yellow flowers alone.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Oleracea vs umbraticola: both may have broad flat leaves, but umbraticola has conspicuous expanded papery ring 0.5–1.5 mm at fruit seam; oleracea no wing. Pilosa: white axillary hair tufts and narrow terete leaves. Phemeranthus longitudinally splits capsule rather than Portulaca's lid.
